title: Multiplexer Module - Band 7 (2600 MHz) for Public Safety Band Filter
subtitle: Design Validation and Performance Characterization
author: Dr. Mei-Ling Chen

sections.1_OBJECTIVE: This document describes the design, simulation, and characterization of a Multiplexer Module filter targeting Band 7 (2600 MHz) for Public Safety Band Filter. The filter is designed on AlN on SiC substrate with a target center frequency of 4424.6 MHz and bandwidth of 181.0 MHz. The objective is to validate that the filter meets the required insertion loss, rejection, and linearity specifications for integration into the Public Safety Band Filter module. This design iteration addresses feedback from the previous revision regarding out-of-band rejection improvements and temperature stability.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Filter Type: Multiplexer Module
- Frequency Band: Band 7 (2600 MHz)
- Application: Public Safety Band Filter
- Substrate: AlN on SiC
- Package: QFN (Quad Flat No-Lead)
- Design Tool: Sonnet EM Suite v16
- Design Center: Singapore RF Lab

This specification applies to all variants of the Multiplexer Module design targeting Band 7 (2600 MHz). Results are used to qualify the design for mass production release.
sections.3_DESIGN_PARAMETERS:
Center Frequency:       4424.6 MHz
Bandwidth (3 dB):       181.0 MHz
Insertion Loss Target:  <= 1.6 dB
Return Loss Target:     >= 9.0 dB
Out-of-Band Rejection:  >= 43.0 dB
Isolation (Duplexer):   >= 29.0 dB
Q Factor:               1001
Temperature Coefficient:-24.0 ppm/°C
Die Size:               1.3 x 2.1 mm
Wafer Size:             6-inch
Number of Resonators:   10
Electrode Material:     Al
Passivation:            Si3N4
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Open Sonnet EM Suite v16 and load the Multiplexer Module template project.
2. Define the substrate stack: AlN on SiC with specified layer thicknesses.
3. Set design targets: center freq 4424.6 MHz, BW 181.0 MHz.
4. Run initial EM simulation with 2D mesh density of 20 cells/wavelength.
5. Optimize resonator geometry using gradient descent (target IL < 1.6 dB).
6. Verify coupling coefficients between resonator stages.
7. Run 3D FEM simulation to account for package parasitics (QFN (Quad Flat No-Lead)).
8. Export GDS-II layout for mask fabrication.
9. Fabricate prototype wafers (6-inch, AlN on SiC).
10. Perform on-wafer probing using Rohde & Schwarz FSW Signal Analyzer.
11. Measure S-parameters (S11, S21, S12, S22) from 100 MHz to 13274 MHz.
12. Compare measured results against simulation and specification limits.
13. Perform temperature cycling (-40°C to +85°C) and re-measure.
14. Document results and generate summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Insertion loss at center frequency shall be <= 1.6 dB
- Return loss in passband shall be >= 9.0 dB
- Out-of-band rejection at +/- 272 MHz offset >= 43.0 dB
- Group delay variation across passband shall be <= 6 ns
- Temperature drift over -40°C to +85°C shall be <= 13.3 MHz
- Power handling shall be >= +31 dBm at 1 dB compression
- ESD tolerance >= 1000 V (HBM)
- Die yield on qualification lot >= 89%
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Measurement Date:       2025-05-22
Devices Tested:         65
Insertion Loss (meas):  1.26 dB
Return Loss (meas):     10.8 dB
Rejection (meas):       46.2 dB
Isolation (meas):       34.3 dB
Q Factor (meas):        1001
Group Delay Variation:  4.7 ns
Power Handling:         +27 dBm
Die Yield:              90.0%

Result Classification:  NEEDS REVIEW
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The Multiplexer Module design demonstrated below-target performance for Band 7 (2600 MHz).
b) Insertion loss met target specification.
c) Out-of-band rejection exceeded the minimum requirement.
d) Simulation-to-measurement correlation was within 3% for all key parameters.
e) No delamination observed after 1000-cycle thermal shock test.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS:
1. Review near-band rejection margin for worst-case temperature.
2. Re-run EM simulation with refined mesh for better accuracy.
3. Schedule follow-up measurement after design tweak.
